EXHIBIT 06: THE TWO CITIES
THE STONE CITY
Concrete, brick, and asphalt.
Abandoned cars rusting in the
streets. Empty storefronts. A
permanent infrastructure left
to die in the Airican sun.
THE WOODEN CITY
A labyrinth of pine and
mahogany shipping crates.
Rich and poor alike frantically
building wooden boxes to pack
up an entire civilization.
THE METAPHOR: Kapuscinski watches the "Wooden City" literally sail away on cargo ships
across the Atlantic, leaving the "Stone City" behind-a poetic distillation of decolonization.

Traditional reporting informs us of what
happened. But narrative journalism--rooted in
rigorous truth, shaped by literary craft, and
filtered through the subjective lens of the
reporter makes us understand what it felt
like to be there.
Closing Thought: The reporter's notebook
remains the ultimate historical
document.
